MARKET.head: Guangdong lychee ice wine sells out online after APEC dinner menu circulates
MARKET.summ: A Guangdong lychee wine became an unexpected online hit after it was served alongside two Changyu wines at the APEC welcome dinner in Shenzhen, with its producer reporting a more than 93,000% jump in revenue at one online store
takeaways: Yueli Lychee Ice Wine from Guangzhou ShunChangYuan saw one online store's revenue rise 93,393.10% after the APEC dinner menu circulated.
The 375ml bottle, 12% alcohol, sells for RMB 174, and one flagship store logged about 5,000 orders within two hours.
The producer has begun emergency restocking as several products are listed as sold out.

MARKET.head: Booze News Weekly Roundup covers Jim Beam pause and record-low wine output
MARKET.summ: This is VinePair’s Booze News Weekly Roundup, where we gather the hottest headlines and product releases every Friday for a snapshot of what’s happening in the beverage alcohol industry. This week, we have updates on the continued production pause at Jim Beam’s main facility, dismal estimates for the 2026 global wine...
takeaways: VinePair's weekly roundup covers the continued production pause at Jim Beam's main facility.
The roundup cites dismal estimates for 2026 global wine production, which remains at a record low.
Other items include product releases and the week's latest beverage alcohol industry headlines.

MARKET.head: Château Lynch-Bages releases limited wines honoring Hong Kong panda twins, funding conservation
MARKET.summ: Bordeaux classified growth Château Lynch-Bages has released limited-edition wines featuring Hong Kong’s first giant panda twins, pairing a celebration of their birth with fundraising for panda conservation
takeaways: Bordeaux estate Château Lynch-Bages released limited-edition 2024 vintage labels featuring Hong Kong's giant panda twins, Jia Jia and De De.
The labels were created with Ocean Park, and a charity auction of large-format bottles will fund the park's panda conservation and education programs.
The wines will be sold in mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau, with Altaya Wines distributing in Hong Kong through retailers including city'super and Watson's Wine.

MARKET.head: DBR Lafite merges China winery and sales under Leo Wang
MARKET.summ: Former Pernod Ricard executive Leo Wang will oversee Domaine de Long Dai and the group’s China sales team as longtime winery chief Charles Treutenaere prepares to leave
takeaways: Domaines Barons de Rothschild Lafite appointed former Pernod Ricard executive Leo Wang to run its China winery and sales as one unit.
Wang becomes managing director of Domaine de Long Dai in Shandong and the Chinese market, splitting time between Shanghai and the estate.
Long Dai general manager Charles Treutenaere, there nine years, leaves at year-end and will help with the handover.

MARKET.head: Melbourne Polytechnic lowers wine degree fees via Commonwealth Supported Places from 2027
MARKET.summ: Melbourne Polytechnic is expanding access to tertiary viticulture and winemaking education through Commonwealth Supported Places in its Bachelor of Agriculture and Technology (Viticulture and Winemaking) from 2027. As Victoria's only provider of undergraduate degrees in viticulture and winemaking, Melbourne Polytechnic “plays a...
takeaways: Melbourne Polytechnic, Victoria's only provider of undergraduate viticulture and winemaking degrees, will offer Commonwealth Supported Places from 2027.
Annual student contribution for the viticulture and winemaking major falls from $23,160 to $4,908 for eligible domestic students.
Victorian Wine Show offers a $5,000 annual scholarship; applications for the 2027 intake are now open.

MARKET.head: WineGB to exhibit English and Welsh wines at Amsterdam trade fair in 2027
MARKET.summ: English and Welsh wine has moved from a niche market to one of the most dynamic cool climate categories in Europe. Producers are gaining international attention for sparkling wines, as
takeaways: WineGB, the English and Welsh wine trade body, will exhibit with the UK government's GREAT programme at Wine Professional in Amsterdam, January 2027.
The stand targets Dutch wine buyers, importers, distributors and sommeliers, showing a range of sparkling, still white, rosé and red wines.

MARKET.head: California Table Grape Commission hires Suzanne Devereaux-McKinstrie as Global Marketing Director
MARKET.summ: The California Table Grape Commission has added Suzanne Devereaux-McKinstrie as its Global Marketing Director for Canada, Mexico, and Central America
takeaways: The California Table Grape Commission named Suzanne Devereaux-McKinstrie its Global Marketing Director for Canada, Mexico, and Central America.
She previously served as CEO of the Center for Produce Safety and as international marketing director for American Pistachio Growers.
She will oversee the commission's marketing programs and work with importers and retailers to increase demand for fresh California table grapes.

MARKET.head: Wine Australia opens funding call for grape and wine innovation projects
MARKET.summ: Wine Australia is today launching a competitive call for innovative eligible projects to secure funding from the Research & Innovation Fund (RIF) which is part of the Australian Wine Future Fund (AWFF). The organisation said innovative and groundbreaking projects tackling the wine industry’s most critical challenges will be...
takeaways: Wine Australia launched an expression of interest for its Research & Innovation Fund, part of the Australian Wine Future Fund.
The fund targets $35 million over five years through grants and partner co-investment for vineyard, product and efficiency projects.
The current round closes 23 December 2026, with assessments in early 2027 and quarterly rounds after that.

MARKET.head: ProWine Mumbai to showcase India's wine and spirits market to global producers
MARKET.summ: India’s growing appeal to international wine and spirits producers will take center stage at ProWine Mumbai this month, as rising disposable incomes, demand for premium drinks and new trade agreements open opportunities in the market
takeaways: ProWine Mumbai runs November 18-19 at Jio World Convention Centre, expecting 200+ exhibitors and 6,000 trade visitors.
Free trade agreements with Australia, the UK and New Zealand, plus EU talks concluded January 2026, are set to cut tariffs on some imports.
Organized by Messe Düsseldorf India and All Things Nice, the show includes ProSpirits and ProWine Zero+ alongside wine.

MARKET.head: Australian white wine exports to China more than double in volume in Q3
MARKET.summ: White wine export volumes to the market more than doubled, rising 143.6%, according to Wine Australia data. The growth comes as Australian producers seek a greater foothold among Chinese white wine drinkers, including consumers exploring alternatives to Burgundy
takeaways: Australian wine export value to mainland China rose 1.9% to A$166.33 million in Q3 2026, against a global decline.
White wine export volumes to mainland China rose 143.6% to 5.26 million liters, while red wine value edged down 0.5%.
South Australia led shipments to China, with value up 32% to A$106.55 million, though nine-month value still fell 10.4%.

CULTURE.head: Guardian tester ranks universal wine glasses from budget to premium
CULTURE.summ:
Searching for a wine glass that can do it all? From short-stemmed to swirlable, dishwasher-friendly to delicate, here’s the glassware that’s a cut above the rest

• The best no- and low-alcohol wines for when you’re...
takeaways: Wine columnist tested universal wine glasses across budgets over several weeks with white, sparkling and red wines.
Glasses were judged on aesthetics, practicality, aroma concentration, visibility, breathing, comfort and enjoyment.
Jancis Robinson co-designed a tulip-shaped universal glass with Richard Brendon, arguing one glass shape suits all wines.

CULTURE.head: ProWine Shanghai shows China's wine buyers seeking distinctive, regional, casual-drinking wines
CULTURE.summ: China’s wine market is becoming more selective, more diverse and less dependent on formal drinking occasions, according to exhibitors at this year’s ProWine Shanghai
takeaways: Exhibitors at ProWine Shanghai say Chinese buyers are becoming more selective, looking beyond quality and price for distinctive wines.
The three-day show drew over 620 exhibitors from 34 countries and regions, plus 21,800 trade visitors.
Wine drinking in China is widening beyond business banquets and gifting into casual restaurants, wine bars and drinking at home.

CULTURE.head: ASVO ratifies four regional directors, adding Mark O'Callaghan and Lane Williams
CULTURE.summ: The Australian Society of Viticulture and Oenology (ASVO) has announced that the appointment of two new directors at its annual general meeting last week “strengthens the board's national presence and builds its depth of skill as the association moves into 2026/27”. “The new board comprises an excellent diversity of experience...
takeaways: The Australian Society of Viticulture and Oenology ratified four regional directors at its annual general meeting last week.
New directors Mark O'Callaghan, a Victorian winemaker and consultant, and Lane Williams, Leeuwin Estate head viticulturist in WA, serve three-year terms.
Alana Seabrook (SA) and Chrissie Smith (NSW/ACT) continue as returning regional directors, with Emily White as executive director since May 2026.

CULTURE.head: Wine's cultural status slipping as sales fall and mocktails rise
CULTURE.summ: I was re-reading an article titled “Is Free Trade Passé?” that the economist Paul Krugman wrote back in 1987 and it got me thinking about what’s happening in the world today. Here is my report. >>><<< Is Free Trade Passé?
takeaways: Columnist compares wine's decline in social status to Paul Krugman's 1987 argument that free trade is no longer the unquestioned default.
He reports that alcoholic beverage sales have fallen sharply and that restaurant tables now often show fewer or no wine bottles.
He uses coffee's shift from default drink to one option among many, including Dutch Bros. drinks, as a parallel for wine.

CULTURE.head: VinePair host Keith Beavers reflects on American wine's 2026 direction
CULTURE.summ: This episode of Wine 101 is brought to you by Wines of Alsace and Alsace Rocks. Tucked between the Vosges Mountains and the Rhine River in northeastern France, Alsace is one of the most distinctive wine regions on earth, and is home to centuries of family winemaking, some of France’s most certifiably organic vineyards, and a...
takeaways: Keith Beavers, host of VinePair's podcast Wine 101, reflects on American wine in 2026.
The episode is sponsored by Wines of Alsace.

CULTURE.head: Alison Smith Story recounts her path into the wine business
CULTURE.summ: This episode of Wine 101 is brought to you by Wines of Alsace and Alsace Rocks. Tucked between the Vosges Mountains and the Rhine River in northeastern France, Alsace is one of the most distinctive wine regions on earth, and is home to centuries of family winemaking, some of France’s most certifiably organic vineyards, and a...
takeaways: Alison Smith Story, of Smith Story Wine Cellars, is the guest on VinePair's podcast Wine 101, hosted by Keith Beavers.
The episode covers how Story came to work in wine and how she fell into the industry.
The sponsor for the episode is Wines of Alsace.

SCIENCE.head: Burgundy estate uses electrical conductivity mapping to read vineyard soils
SCIENCE.summ: Electrical conductivity maps can reveal striking differences beneath seemingly uniform vineyards, but understanding what those differences mean is far more complicated
takeaways: Domaine du Cellier aux Moines in Givry, Burgundy, uses electrical conductivity (EC) mapping to locate soil differences guiding vineyard work.
Owner Philippe Pascal, an agronomist and former LVMH executive, bought the 12th-century estate in 2004 and began EC mapping in 2021.
In the 2026 vintage, a tressed Pinot Noir parcel reached 13.6% potential alcohol versus 14.5% for a conventionally trimmed neighbour.

SCIENCE.head: AWRI urges users to update its free agrochemical and MRL search app
SCIENCE.summ: 9 November 2026 The Australian Wine Research Institute has updated the version of the AWRI Agrochemical & MRL Search app on both the Apple App … more
takeaways: The Australian Wine Research Institute has updated its AWRI Agrochemical & MRL Search app on Apple and Google app stores.
The free app gives rapid access to information from the 'Agrochemicals registered for use in Australian viticulture' booklet.
Users must perform an app update to keep receiving updates for the app, and the AWRI helpdesk can assist.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Vinography’s 2026 Gift Guide for Discerning Wine Lovers
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Buying a gift for a serious wine lover can be maddening. The more devoted they are, the better the odds
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow

NEWSLETTERS.head: Beaujolais Anew
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The 2026 release of that wine we love to hate and hate to love, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Beaujolais Nouveau was pushed onto the international stage by vignerons in the 1950s and by négociants like Georges Duboeuf from the 1970s.
Beaujolais Nouveau is released worldwide on the third Thursday of November, and Gamay is its grape.
Producers like Marcel Lapierre in Morgon label crus-origin wines as Vin de France due to French labeling laws, calling theirs "Raisins Gaulois.".

NEWSLETTERS.head: Cabernet Franc in the Press: November 2026
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Livermore wins Region of the Year, Wine Spectator profiles Loire Cabernet Franc, Decanter takes a cross-border look at Ontario and New York, and much more
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Wine Enthusiast named California's Livermore Valley its 2026 American Wine Region of the Year in its annual Wine Star Awards.
Livermore Valley is known for Sauvignon Blanc and Cabernet Franc, which its regional association named its signature white and red varieties in February 2025.
A Cabernet Franc claimed top honours at Maryland's Governor's Cup, per the newsletter.

NEWSLETTERS.head: More Than Skin Deep: A Grape with a Colourful Past
NEWSLETTERS.summ: A colourful tale of the grape that was born to dye and the father-son team behind it
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: Pinot Noir and Pinot Meunier, Champagne's black grapes, have colourless juice, so they can make white 'Blanc de Noirs' Champagne.
Teinturier grapes have red flesh; Garnacha Tintorera, also called Alicante Bouschet, was bred by Henri Bouschet in the late 1800s from Petit Bouschet and Garnacha Tinto.
Pago Casa Gran 'Reposo' 2024 from Valencia, Spain is a blend of 60% Garnacha Tintorera, 20% Syrah and 20% Monastrell.

NEWSLETTERS.head: What the Hell Do They Mean?
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Let’s play wine tasting note bingo, here’s TMC’s handy guide
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Tasting-note jargon like 'minerality' is described as a vague term used to avoid saying what a wine actually tastes like.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Burgundy Region Quietly Absorbing This Year’s Rising Prices
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Discover how the Burgundy wine market quietly absorbs rising prices in 2026, revealing new trends and steady demand for fine wine collectors
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: Comité des Vins de Bourgogne figures show Burgundy white wine sales rose 0.4 per cent in the year to July 2026, while red fell 4.9 per cent.
Mâconnais bulk prices fell: Mâcon-Villages Blanc down 9 per cent and Bourgogne Blanc down 13 per cent, per regional figures reported in March.
Pouilly-Fuissé's 2024 reference price was about €817 a hectolitre, versus roughly €3,050 for Puligny-Montrachet.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Many Sins Of Wine Critics
NEWSLETTERS.summ: In the exciting (other adjectives are available) times we’re living in, we’re often told that writing is passé, people just don’t bother reading words anymore. A few journalistic outlets, especially in the financial press, seem to have finally come clean about the seriousness of their reporting, by auto-summarising their pieces...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin argues wine critics should be only slightly more knowledgeable than their target audience, not supertasters writing for ordinary shoppers.
Atkin says conflicts of interest extend beyond payment to dining, friendships and shared politics, and that disclosure can encourage more self-interested reviews.
Atkin criticises the brief 30-second tasting ritual, often applied to lineups of tens or over a hundred wines, as too little time to judge a wine.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Find Rare Shizz With Orpheus Alerts!
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Some (more!) exciting news, folks: As many of you already know, sometimes wines get featured on here that are pretty rare. I’m talking about the kind of stuff that either doesn’t make it to the big platforms, or, if it does, is either priced astronomically or is gone in milliseconds. Understandably, that can be somewhat […]...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: 1WineDude is partnering with Orpheus Alerts, part of Orpheus Intelligence Labs Inc., to help buyers find rare wines.
Orpheus monitors sources like local-language catalogues, merchant inventories, auction and consignment notices, and private cellar sales.
Users create alerts using natural-language descriptions or images, and Orpheus notifies them when a matching wine is available and connects them to the seller.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Roadshow Review: Spain Brings Value Wines to China
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Does any nation offer better wine value than Spain? This seems obvious to French bottlers, who import major amounts of Spanish wine each year. Per
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jim Boyce
takeaways: Spain ranked fifth by volume in China last year, narrowly behind Italy but a quarter of leader Australia, per WBO stats.
Spain dropped to sixth by value in China, below New Zealand, with only Chile's per-liter value lower among the top eight sources.
The Wines From Castilla, La Mancha Roadshow stopped in Beijing, with Guangzhou next on November 6, aiming to lift Spain's underperforming China sales.

NEWSLETTERS.head: A deeper look at underwater wine aging
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Is a wine from the depths ‘better’ or does it depend on the boat?
NEWSLETTERS.author: Miquel Hudin
takeaways: Attis, a winery owned by the Fariña family near O Grove in Galicia, ages its Albariño 'Mar' bottles underwater in the estuary.
The Attis Albariño 'Mar' is aged five months under water at 13-16C, versus the 'Standard' bottling of about 120,000 bottles annually.
